case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 5th day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4692 of 2005 with Civil Revision No.4688 of 2005)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. These two appeals, by leave, are from the judgment and order dated 5th day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4692 of 2005 heard analogously with Civil Revision No. 4688 of 2005 making the Rules absolute issued in both the revisions.

2. Respondent Nos. 1-9 as the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No. 458 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Shibgonj Bogra for declaration of title. From the facts as stated in the leave petition, it appears that during the pendency of the aforesaid suit, the plaintiffs filed another suit being Other Suit No. 110 of 1985 in the same Court for recovery of possession.

3. The case of the plaintiffs in both the suits, in short, was that Moshor Fakir, lit their predecessor, acquired the suit land from landlord-Rafatullah Mondal and had been in possession thereof since 1338 BS as korfa tenant and C.S. Khatian No. 93 in respect of suit land was correctly prepared I in the name of Moshor Fakir. Moshor Fakir while possessing the suit land died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his legal heirs and since his death, the plaintiffs had been possessing the same. The defendants had no right, title and possession in the suit land. On 01.11.1984, defendant No. 2 disclosed to plaintiff No.1 that defendant No.1 executed and registered a kabala in his favour in respect of the suit land and MRR Khatian in respect of the suit land was prepared in the name of defendant No.1, Defendant No. 2 further disclosed that he would build a pucca house therein, Thereafter, plaintiff No.1 went to the local Tashil office and came to know for the first time that the name of defendant No.1 was included in the MRR Khatian along with the name of the plaintiffs father; hence the suit.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Rafatullah Mondal was the landlord and Moshor Fakir was a korfa tenant under him in the suit land. Moshor Fakir 3rd Falgun, 1338 BS executed an 'istafapatra' in respect of the suit land in favour of the landlord and transferred his right, title and interest in his favour and he (landlord) took khas possession of the suit land. Thereafter, Rafatullah Mondal on 19.11.1942 transferred 91 decimals land including the suit land by a kabala in favour of his son, Tasiruddin Mondal and thereafter.

<u>5. Tasiruddin Mondal transferred the same to defendant No.1 by a kabala dated 18.02.1948. Defendant No.1 on 02.08.1960 transferred 9¾ decimals land from Plot No. 381 to Monsur Ali Mondal and he had been possessing the same. Defendant No.1 transferred 8 decimals land to defendant No.2 by a registered kabala. Said Monsur Ali Mondal transferred 93/4 decimals land to defendant No. 2 and thus defendant No. 2 acquired 173/4 decimals land and he had been possessing the same. Defendant No. 2 built a pucca house long before filing the suit, The defendants had been running business in a portion of the house. The plaintiffs had no right, title in the suit land and the defendants did not dispossess them there from on 18.11.1948. The suit land was not properly valued and sufficiently stamped, so, the suit was liable to be dismissed.</u>

6. Both the suits were heard analogously and the learned Assistant Judge by a common judgment dated 24.07.1989 (separate decrees were drawn and signed) decreed the suits, Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the defendants preferred Other Appeal Nos.142 of 1989 and 147 of 1989 respectively before the District Judge, Bogra. The Appellate Court by a common judgment dated 30.06.1992(separate decrees were drawn and signed) remanded the suits to the trial Court for fresh trial. After remand, the suits were heard afresh and the learned Assistant Judge by the judgment dated 13.05.2004 (separate decrees were drawn and signed) decreed both the suits. Against the judgment   and decree of the trial Court, the predecessor of appellant Nos. 1-4 and 5 preferred Other Appeal Nos.68 and 72 of 2004 respectively before the District Judge, Bogra. The learned Joint District Judge 2nd Court, Bogra by a common judgment dated 05.10.2005(separate decrees were drawn and signed) allowed both the appeals and reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed   the suit, Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs  filed Civil Revision Nos.4688 of 2005 and 4692 of 2005 before the High Court Division and a learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rules absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1807 and 1808 of 2008 and leave was granted by this Court to consider the submissions made on their behalf by their learned Advocate-on-Record which are as follows:

"Mr. Md. Mazibar Rahman, learned Advocate-on-Record„ appearing for the petitioners submitted that the defendants have proved their case and on the other hand the plaintiffs failed to prove the case of possession inasmuch as for non-impleading the necessary parties the suit flied by the said plaintiffs is not maintainable, as it has been clearly found by the learned District Judge while disposing of the Appeals; being Other Appeal No. 68 of 2004 and Other Appeal No. 72 of 2004 heard analogously and passed the judgment and decree reversing the judgment and decree passed analogously on 13.05.2004 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Shibgonj, Bogra in Other Suit No. 45 8 of 1994 and Other Suit No. 110 of 1985 and the High Court Division without reversing the findings of the Appellate Court arrived at a wrong and erroneous decision on a total misconception and non-consideration of the case; that the learned joint District judge being the last Court of findings of fact arrived at a clear finding in reversing the judgments and decrees of the trial Court and on the other hand the High Court Division reversing all the findings of the Appellate Court arrived a wrong and erroneous decision which is also perverse. The learned Advocate-on-Record further submitted that the plaintiffs having been failed to prove the case and on the other hand the defendants proved the case including the Estofapatra given by Moshor Fakir in favour Rafatullah and thereafter, the Rafatullah transferred the suit land on 19.11.1942 in favour of his son Tasimuddin and since then there is the continuation of possession of the defendants and the High Court Division having failed to consider the same the impugned judgment and order dated 05.05.2008 is liable to be set aside, The learned Advocate-on-Record finally submitted that in view of the facts that the plaintiffs did not file the suit in time and it is the clear findings of the appellate Court that ‘‘ নথি পর্যালোচনায় দেখা যায় যে, বাদীগণ সময়মত মামলা দায়ের করেন নাই। তাই বাদীদের মামলাটি তামাদী দোষে অচল।" and the said findings having not been reversed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, the finding that " বিবাদীগণ বাদীকে নালিশী জমি হইতে বেদখল করে নাই।" have also not been reversed and as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside,"

7. Mr. Kamal-ul Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the 'appellants, has reiterated the submissions on which leave was granted and in support of his submissions, he has referred to the materials on record including the plaint, the written statement and the deposition of the witnesses.

8. Mr. Nurul Islam Sujan, learned Counsel, for the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

9. The judgment and decree impugned before the High Court Division was the judgment and decree of reversal, so it was its incumbent duty to see whether the Appellate Court being the last Court of fact adverted to the findings of the trial Court in reversing its judgment and decree. Let us see whether the High Court Division did the said job in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restoring those of the trial Court.

10. From the judgment of the Appellate Court, it appears that the main question to be decided in the suit was whether Moshor Fakir surrendered the suit land to Rafatullah Mondal and whether after surrender Rafatullah Mondal got possession thereof, The Appellate Court considering the evidence on record came to the clear finding that PW1-Masiruddin Fakir admit-ted in his cross-examination that there were homestead of the defendants in the suit land and presently, he lives at Sadullahpur and one of his brothers lives 1/2 miles away. The Appellate Court further found that from the plaint, it appeared that out of the three sons of Moshor Fakir, plaintiff No.1 was Masir Fakir, plaintiff No. 2 was Abdul Fakir and plaintiff No. 3 was Dilbar Fakir and their addresses were shown at Sadullahpur and the addresses of their two sisters, Maziran and Sutki, were shown at their husband's addresses, so at the time of filing Title Suit No.458 of 1984 for declaration of title, the plaintiffs did not reside in the suit land.

<u>11. The Appellate Court further found that in the plaint, the plaintiff did not say as to how they exercised their right of possession in the suit land. Though the plaintiff claimed that the defendants dispossessed them from the suit land on 18.11.1984. from the testimonies of the plaintiffs' witnesses, it was clearly proved that long before the said date of alleged dispossession, the plaintiffs were not in possession of the suit land. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the PWs proved that the defendants had been in possession of the suit land long before the filing of the suit, the defendants' witnesses also said that defendant No. 1 had been in possession of the suit land since 30/35 years, PW1 in his cross-examination stated that Refatullah used to possess the suit land, The Appellate Court further observed to the effect that " উভয় পরে সাক্ষীদের সাক্ষ্য পর্যালোচনায় ইহা স্পষ্ট বুঝা যায় যে, ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখের বহু পূর্ব হইতে নালিশী জমিতে ১নং বিবাদী গেন্দালা দখলকার আছে। অর্থাৎ ১৮/১১/৮৪ তারিখে বাদীকে বেদখলের আর্জি বর্ণিত বক্তব্য সঠিক আছে। The Appellate Court further found that the plaintiff claimed that Moshor Fakir did not give ‘ইস্তফা’ of the suit land to Rafatullah and although the defendants spoke about the ‘ইস্তফা’ they did not file the same, yet PW1 admitted in his cross-examination that the suit land used to be possessed by Rafatullah. The Appellate Court also found that from the evidence of PW1 it was clearly proved that Rafatullah transferred the suit land in favour of his son, Tasiruddin on 19.11.1942 and had he not been in possession of the suit land, he would not have transferred the same in the name of his son and that it was not a believable story that in 1942, Rafatullah would create an ineffective deed in favour of his son thinking about the present suit and that no body would create a fake deed in favour of his son. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that since it was proved from the testimonies of the PWs that the plaintiffs had not been in possession of the suit land for a long time and they had left the suit property long before it could be clearly understood that Moshor Fakir gave 'Estafa' of the suit land in favour of Rafatullah. Therefore, Rafatullah had the right to transfer the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that from the documentary evidence, it appeared that except the C.S. and the MIRR khatian, the plaintiffs filed only one rent receipt and that also after the filing of the suit, on the other hand, on behalf of the defendants, besides the deeds dated 19.11.1942 in favour of Tasiruddin by Rafatullah, dated 18.02.1948 in favour of Gendala by Moshor and the deed dated 02.08.1960 in favour of Shahjalal, mutation khatian, DCR, 15 rent receipts and the other khatians were filed which also proved the defendants' possession in the suit land. The Appellate Court further observed that the witnesses might tell lie or wrong, but the circumstances do not, the circumstances of case proved that the suit land reverted back to Rafatullah and he transferred the same in favour of his son who in turn sold the same in favour of Gendela, defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 2 and Mansur purchased the same land from Gendela.</u>

12. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the plaintiffs first filed the suit for declaration of title and then filed the second suit for eviction of the defendants from the suit land which proved that the defendants did not dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land, so the plaintiffs had no reasonable cause to file the suit for eviction and basically the plaintiffs were required to file a suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession, the plaintiffs' suits were not maintainable in law, The Appellate Court further found that the deeds being dated it 19.11.1942, 18.02.1948 and 02.08.1960 were very old documents and there was no reason to say that those were ineffective deeds, The Appellate Court also found that from the evidence of PW 1, it was clear that the plaintiffs transferred a portion of the suit land and from the two plaints, it appeared that the transferees from them were not made parties in the suit, so the plaintiffs had no right to pray for declaration of title in respect of the entire suit property and the suit was also bad for defect of party. The Appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs had no title and possession in the suit land and accordingly reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court and dismissed the suit.

13. The High Court Division in setting aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court did not at all advert any findings of the Appellate Court as noted down hereinbefore. It further appears that in coming to the above noted findings, the Appellate Court discussed the evidence both oral and documentary, but the High Court Division failed to consider these findings of the Appellate Court with reference to the evidence on record and also failed to pin point how and why the Appellate Court committed the error in reversing those of the trial Court and it, in a very slip shod manner, just restored those of the trial Court. Thus, the High Court Division failed to exercise the jurisdiction vested in it under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We have gone through the pleading of the respective party and the evidence, we found the findings and the observation of the Appellate Court based on correct appreciation of the evidence.

14. In view of the above, the impugned judgment and order cannot be sustained and accordingly, the same is set aside, the appeals are allowed. There will no order as to cost.

End.
